subject: biology
summary: Most biology cards are clean: a short typed question, a correctly chosen and tightly cropped diagram, and a tick-list scheme that plainly answers the part asked. The recurring fault is examiner mark shorthand leaking into a grey note under the scheme (e.g. '(6(3) + 2)', '(7+7+2+4(1))', '(3(4) + 3(3) + 3(2))') which describes the WHOLE question's arithmetic, not this card, and on those cards the tick points carry no marks at all. Whole short-question cards (Q1-style) flatten the (a)/(i)/(ii) hierarchy so sub-parts sit further left than their parents, and the scheme lists every alternative answer as its own tick box. One card (2020 OL Q5(d)) shows the question only as a crop of the full Q5 grid, which is tiny on a phone and whose scheme gives one answer with no hint which box it belongs to. Genetics notation loses its superscripts (XNXn, XnY_).

issues.title: Whole-question mark shorthand shown under single-part schemes
issues.detail: A grey note reads 'The examiner marks the first correct answers higher than the rest (6(3) + 2) — so what these are worth depends on how many you got.' The bracketed sum is raw SEC shorthand for the entire question (20 marks for Q3, 20 for Q5, etc.), not this card: card 6 is a 3-mark part showing '6(3) + 2'; card 9 is a 7-mark part showing '7+7+2+4(1)'; card 4 is 10 marks showing '3(5) + 6(2)'; card 12 is 24 marks showing '3(4) + 3(3) + 3(2)' which sums to 27. On these cards no tick point has a mark chip, so the student cannot tell what anything is worth.
issues.suggested_fix: Translate the shorthand into plain words scoped to this part ('first 3 correct points 4 marks each, next 3 worth 3, ...') or put a mark chip on each point; never print the raw bracket sum, and never print the whole question's sum on a part card.

issues.title: Question shown only as a tiny crop of the whole Q5 grid
issues.detail: 2020 OL Q5(d) has no typed question at all; the question area is a crop of the entire Q5 (instruction, word list, all eight cell pictures with boxes (a) to (g)). On the phone the instruction and word list render at roughly 6-7px, far below body text. The card is for (d) only but nothing tells the student that (d) is the bottom-left picture, and the scheme is a lone 'Red blood cell' tick with no part label and no marks, on a card headed 7 marks.
issues.suggested_fix: Type the instruction and the word list as text, crop only the cell picture for (d) (or make the card the whole Q5 with a seven-row answer list '(a) Cheek cell ... (g) Neuron'), and fix the mark total to match.

issues.title: Part hierarchy inverted and alternatives listed as separate ticks on whole-question cards
issues.detail: On 2012 OL Q1 the sub-parts (i)/(ii) are flush left while their parents (b), (c), (d), (e) are indented further right, so the list reads backwards; the orange underline also stops mid-sentence on several lines. In the scheme, alternative answers for one part are separate tick boxes ('(c) — Keratin', '(c) — Myosin', '(c) — Collagen'; five separate '(d)' rows) with no 'any one' wording, '(ii) — Crisps' has lost its '(a)', a stray 'not spread' note floats above the Butter row, and no row shows marks. It is 16 tick boxes for 7 one-word answers.
issues.suggested_fix: Indent (i)/(ii) under their letter; group the scheme by part with one row per part: '(c) Any one: keratin / myosin / collagen — 3m'.

issues.title: Genotype notation flattened
issues.detail: Sex-linked genotypes lose their superscripts and are inconsistent: 'Son — XNY-', 'Mother — XNXN or XNXn', 'Father — XnY_', 'Son gets Y_ from sperm'. A student could read XNXN as four letters, and 'Y-' vs 'Y_' looks like a typo.
issues.suggested_fix: Render with real superscripts (X^N X^n, X^n Y) or show a crop of the official scheme's cross diagram.

issues.title: Redundant or broken helper text
issues.detail: Card 7 shows an 'Also on the diagram' box reading 'Cotyledon — Cotyledon' and 'Embryo — Embryo' (label equals answer, pure noise). Card 8's bottom summary bar reads 'Bacteria — Monera · Protista · Rhizopus — Fungi', dropping 'Amoeba —'. Card 3's first scheme row 'Penis, testis, urethra and sperm duct 6m (Any one missing only 3 marks)' is the diagram mark but is not labelled as such and then the six labels repeat below. Card 1 keeps the stem 'Write notes on three of the following topics:' though only one topic is on the card, and its heading 'Any 3 of these — 4 then 3 then 3 marks' is cryptic.
issues.suggested_fix: Hide 'Also on the diagram' when label and answer are identical; prefix the diagram mark with 'Diagram shows:'; reword the stem to 'Write notes on: Vaccination'; say 'first point 4 marks, next two 3 marks each'.

issues.title: Large dead space and odd order on the phone
issues.detail: On every phone card there is a blank band of roughly 200-400px between 'Open original paper' and 'Your answer', and the scheme always sits below an empty answer box, so the scheme never shares a screen with the question. Short cards look half empty.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the minimum height on the question pane on phones and collapse the answer box once the scheme is revealed.

good_examples.why: Clear typed question, large legible ear diagram, three labelled 1-mark answers A/B/C.
One-line question and a clean 'Any 4 of these — 3 marks each' point list.
Stem, pedigree chart with key and three 3-mark criteria all read cleanly.
